findings: At fixed group count, increasing features per group from 2 to 8 increased stage-2 terms/output 4x and increased isolated stage-2 Q.ANT error at every tested group count.
For width 2, increasing groups 8→16→28 reduced stage-1 MAE 0.01631→0.01375→0.01037.
The lowest mean end-to-end logit error among the six tested architectures was 28x2 at 0.06289.
The 28x8 architecture had the highest mean reference accuracy (0.86067) but substantially larger end-to-end logit error (0.10118), demonstrating an accuracy-versus-numerical-compatibility trade-off.
interpretation: The factorial intervention breaks the fixed-width coupling exposed by Exp026 and supports separately measurable stage-1 and stage-2 accumulation effects on the Q.ANT CPU backend.
next_research_direction: Fit a preregistered two-variable compatibility model on Exp027 and test it on unseen group-width combinations.
limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
The factorial grid contains six architectures and should be treated as an initial calibration set.
